parentReview.scopeOfAcceptance: Accepted for version-fidelity CHECKS: asking of a generated world whether a given block could have existed in Beta 1.7.3. NOT accepted for gameplay enforcement, item/recipe availability or inventory rules, because this tool recovers block NAMES only and deliberately does not pair them with numeric ids.
knownLimitations: Numeric ids are not paired with names by this tool; where ids appear in the checks they come from this project's earlier, separately recorded evidence.
83 names were recovered from 108 string loads in the block initialiser; the other 25 strings are not lowerCamelCase block names, but that filter is a heuristic and is the weakest step here.
This covers Beta 1.7.3 only. The same tool would need to be run against each other version's jar before the check can be made version-aware for them, and Mojang does not publish every jar.

The palette covers only the blocks registered in the main block class (uu.class). Cocoa, for example, does not occur in that class at all, although Beta 1.7.3 certainly had it, so the set is INCOMPLETE. This makes the check conservative rather than wrong: a block that is absent from the palette AND absent from the modern-to-legacy mapping table is reported UNKNOWN and is never suppressed, so the worst case is an unreported defect rather than a wrongly removed historical block.
